liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **El Paso** (1 review): The arrangement is very cool, though Bobby hadn't yet worked out the real lyrics [13]
- **Rosalie McFall** (1 review): Described as stunning [14]
- **Deep Elem Blues** (1 review): Played in a laid-back way [14]
- **To Lay Me Down** (1 review): Jerry's playing on this song is singled out as outstanding [6]

## Setlist highlights

- **Tell It To Me**: rare: 3 archived performances [15]
- **Drink Up and Go Home**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [15]
- **A Voice From On High**: rare: 5 archived performances [15]
- **Swing Low Sweet Chariot**: rare: 13 archived performances [15]
- **Ballad of Casey Jones**: rare: 3 archived performances [15]

## The recordings

- **gd70-08-05.sbd.jupile.17271.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 15 songs; 62 min; rated 4.29/5 by 28 [1]. Said about its sound: Mix is slightly off but audio quality is excellent; the mandolin sits prominently, almost too loud; Reviewer finds the recording poor because the level was recorded too low; Recording quality could be somewhat better [1][5][6][8][9][13][14]
- **gd1970-08-05.sbd.thecore.4941.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 15 songs; 63 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: Vocal mix is low throughout; slight tape noise and static late in set 2 [2]

## Around the show

- Delivered in a laid-back, almost devotional mood; the audience sounds very small [5]
- Reviewer believes the mandolin player is Jerry rather than David Nelson [8]
- Reviewer thought the mandolinist was Dawg, and suspects Dick's notes came from the tape, not attendance [9]
- Attendee says David Nelson played mandolin and was fantastic [10]
- Dick's notes say Jerry played mandolin, but reviewer thinks Jerry stayed on guitar all set [12]
- Reviewer ranks it as an easy pick among the Dead's 1970 acoustic sets [5]
- Rates it among the best of the 1970 acoustic Dead sets heard, perhaps the best [8]
- Attendee says he later missed the acoustic shows of the early seventies [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-08-05.sbd.jupile.17271.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Andy Lemieux and Joe Jupile; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Points to Dick Latvala's own notebook notes on the show and recording; Directs listeners to Dick Latvala's notebook notes on this show; Newer copy per Andy Lemieux: MSR to cassette, three generations, then DAT and CDR; a significant upgrade over older copy [1][7][11]
- **gd1970-08-05.sbd.thecore.4941.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>MR>PCM>D>CD>EAC>SHN [2]. Also: Normalization and minor edits were done with Sound Forge [2]
